title: Make git log answer the question you actually asked
summary: The default git log is nearly useless on a real repository. Learn the eight flags that turn it into a precision instrument, and build the one view you will use every day.
mental_model: `git log` is a filter plus a formatter over the commit graph. Every flag either narrows which commits are listed, or changes how each one is printed. Learn one of each and the rest compose.

steps.title: The default, and why nobody uses it
steps.why: Six lines per commit, no shape, no files. On a repository with ten thousand commits this tells you almost nothing. Every flag below exists because of this output.

steps.title: One line each, with the shape
steps.why: `--oneline --graph --decorate --all` is the workhorse. It shows every branch, where they diverged, where they merged, and which refs point where — in one screen.
steps.expect: A visible fork and merge, with branch names marked.

steps.title: What changed, without the noise
steps.why: `--stat` adds a file summary per commit; `-p` shows the full patch. Use --stat to scan, -p when you have narrowed it down to one or two commits.

steps.title: Filter by who, when and what
steps.why: These three narrow a huge history fast. `--since` accepts human phrases, `--author` matches a substring, and `-- <path>` limits to a file. They compose freely.
steps.expect: The last one shows only the two commits touching pump.py.

steps.title: Hide the merge noise, or show only it
steps.why: `--no-merges` gives the human-written commits; `--first-parent` follows only the main line, treating each merge as a single event. On a busy repository this is the difference between readable and unreadable.

steps.title: Build your own format
steps.why: `--pretty=format:` takes placeholders: %h short hash, %s subject, %an author, %ar relative date, %d refs. This is how every fancy log alias you have seen is built.
steps.expect: A compact table you could paste into a release note.

steps.title: Save it as the alias you will actually use
steps.why: Nobody types forty characters twice. Alias the combination you like and it becomes muscle memory.

verify.label: you saved a graph log alias
first-parent history is five commits — the merge counts once
full history is seven commits, including both sides of the merge
path-limited history isolates the two pump commits

pitfalls: `git log <path>` without `--` breaks if a branch shares the name of a file. Always write `git log -- <path>`.
`--since` filters by commit date, which rebasing changes. For 'what shipped last week', tags are more reliable than dates.
`--graph` output is only meaningful with `--all` or an explicit set of branches — otherwise you see one line and no shape.
`-p` on a merge commit shows nothing by default. Use `-m` or `--first-parent -p` to see merge diffs.
cheatsheet: the full patch of one commit
the main line only, merges as single events
